description: Conformance test vectors for SPEC.md section 7. Covers the base GHMM/HMM categories over the classical checksum family (transition_matrices/classical.py), whose oracles are closed-form: state count n * m + 1, stationary distribution, and word probabilities by phase alignment. Every expected value here is derived from those closed forms rather than captured from an implementation. See CONFORMANCE.md for the encoding decisions SPEC section 7 leaves open, and for what is not yet covered.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of the checksum process, RRXOR: n=2, m=2, uniform rows.
test_vectors.notes: Closed form: 1/(n+1) = 1/3 on the seed state, and P(sum of the first i random symbols = r mod 2) / 3 on state (i, r). The 5 states are ordered as the seed state followed by (phase, residue) pairs, phase-major.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of the checksum process, biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4].
test_vectors.notes: Closed form: 1/(n+1) = 1/3 on the seed state, and P(sum of the first i random symbols = r mod 2) / 3 on state (i, r). The 5 states are ordered as the seed state followed by (phase, residue) pairs, phase-major.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of the checksum process, n=1, m=2 -- emit a random bit, then repeat it.
test_vectors.notes: Closed form: 1/(n+1) = 1/2 on the seed state, and P(sum of the first i random symbols = r mod 2) / 2 on state (i, r). The 3 states are ordered as the seed state followed by (phase, residue) pairs, phase-major.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of the checksum process, n=2, m=3 over a ternary alphabet.
test_vectors.notes: Closed form: 1/(n+1) = 1/3 on the seed state, and P(sum of the first i random symbols = r mod 3) / 3 on state (i, r). The 7 states are ordered as the seed state followed by (phase, residue) pairs, phase-major.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of the checksum process, n=3, m=2 -- a three-bit block plus its parity.
test_vectors.notes: Closed form: 1/(n+1) = 1/4 on the seed state, and P(sum of the first i random symbols = r mod 2) / 4 on state (i, r). The 7 states are ordered as the seed state followed by (phase, residue) pairs, phase-major.

test_vectors.description: RRXOR observation distribution from the default (stationary) initial state.
test_vectors.notes: The rows sum to 1, so this is the HMM special case of SPEC 3.2.1 with w = 1 and the canonical state representative equal to an ordinary distribution over states. Uniform rows and a symmetric parity make both symbols equally likely at every phase.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the stationary state, biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4].
test_vectors.notes: P(x) = [sum_i probs[i][x] + P(sum of all n symbols = x)] / (n + 1): each random phase contributes its own row, and the checksum phase contributes the running-sum distribution.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the stationary state, n=2, m=3 over a ternary alphabet.
test_vectors.notes: The same closed form with m = 3, so the alphabet and the modulus are both 3.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the stationary state, n=3, m=2 -- a three-bit block plus its parity.
test_vectors.notes: Three random rows plus a parity phase, so the average leans on all three rows.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (0, 0), where the seed state emits row 0 of probs.
test_vectors.notes: State (0, 0) of the process biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4]: the seed state emits row 0 of probs.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (1, 1), where a phase-1 state emits row 1 of probs, whatever its residue.
test_vectors.notes: State (1, 1) of the process biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4]: a phase-1 state emits row 1 of probs, whatever its residue.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (2, 0), where a checksum state emits its residue with probability 1.
test_vectors.notes: State (2, 0) of the process biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4]: a checksum state emits its residue with probability 1.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (2, 1), where a checksum state emits its residue with probability 1.
test_vectors.notes: State (2, 1) of the process biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4]: a checksum state emits its residue with probability 1.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (1, 2), where a phase-1 state emits row 1, so the residue is irrelevant.
test_vectors.notes: State (1, 2) of the process n=2, m=3 over a ternary alphabet: a phase-1 state emits row 1, so the residue is irrelevant.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from the pure state (2, 1), where a phase-2 state emits row 2 of probs.
test_vectors.notes: State (2, 1) of the process n=3, m=2 -- a three-bit block plus its parity: a phase-2 state emits row 2 of probs.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from a state representative scaled by 1.0.
test_vectors.notes: SPEC 3.4 divides by eta . w, so every positive multiple of a representative is the same predictive state. The three checksum_obs_dist_scaled_* vectors differ only in the scale of their input and share this expected output.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from a state representative scaled by 7.5.
test_vectors.notes: SPEC 3.4 divides by eta . w, so every positive multiple of a representative is the same predictive state. The three checksum_obs_dist_scaled_* vectors differ only in the scale of their input and share this expected output.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution from a state representative scaled by 0.001.
test_vectors.notes: SPEC 3.4 divides by eta . w, so every positive multiple of a representative is the same predictive state. The three checksum_obs_dist_scaled_* vectors differ only in the scale of their input and share this expected output.

test_vectors.description: A state update from a rescaled stationary state returns the same canonical posterior.
test_vectors.notes: SPEC 3.5 renormalizes by eta T^(x) . w, so the posterior is scale-free, and SPEC 7.1.2 serializes it in canonical form -- here an ordinary sum-to-1 distribution, since w = 1.

test_vectors.description: From the pure state (0, 0), observing 0 moves to (1, 0).
test_vectors.notes: The process is unifilar, so a pure state stays pure: (0, 0) plus symbol 0 gives (1, 0). A random phase carries the running sum to (r + x) mod 2; a checksum phase returns to the seed state.

test_vectors.description: From the pure state (0, 0), observing 1 moves to (1, 1).
test_vectors.notes: The process is unifilar, so a pure state stays pure: (0, 0) plus symbol 1 gives (1, 1). A random phase carries the running sum to (r + x) mod 2; a checksum phase returns to the seed state.

test_vectors.notes: The process is unifilar, so a pure state stays pure: (2, 1) plus symbol 1 gives (0, 0). A random phase carries the running sum to (r + x) mod 2; a checksum phase returns to the seed state.

test_vectors.notes: The process is unifilar, so a pure state stays pure: (1, 0) plus symbol 0 gives (0, 0). A random phase carries the running sum to (r + x) mod 2; a checksum phase returns to the seed state.

test_vectors.description: State update from the stationary mixture after observing 0, RRXOR: n=2, m=2, uniform rows.
test_vectors.notes: The phase is unknown under the stationary state, so the posterior is the prior-weighted mixture of each state's successor, renormalized: mass on (i+1, (r+x) mod m) is proportional to pi[(i, r)] * probs[i][x], and mass on the seed state comes from the one checksum state whose residue is the observed symbol.

test_vectors.description: P(empty sequence) under the process RRXOR: n=2, m=2, uniform rows.
test_vectors.notes: SPEC 3.6 defines P(empty sequence) = 1.

test_vectors.description: P(0) under the process RRXOR: n=2, m=2, uniform rows.
test_vectors.notes: Summed over the 3 phase alignments, weighted by the stationary probability of each initial state. An alignment contributes the product of its random-phase emission probabilities, or 0 if a checksum position disagrees with the running sum there.

test_vectors.description: P(00100) under the process RRXOR: n=2, m=2, uniform rows.
test_vectors.notes: Forbidden word. Every one of the 3 phase alignments fails: no placement of block boundaries makes each block's last symbol the sum of that block's random symbols mod m, so the probability is exactly 0. Note this is a zero probability, not a zero-denominator update, which SPEC 7.4 puts outside conformance.

test_vectors.description: P(01) under the process biased RRXOR: n=2, m=2, rows [0.3, 0.7] and [0.6, 0.4].
test_vectors.notes: Summed over the 3 phase alignments, weighted by the stationary probability of each initial state. An alignment contributes the product of its random-phase emission probabilities, or 0 if a checksum position disagrees with the running sum there.

test_vectors.notes: Summed over the 2 phase alignments, weighted by the stationary probability of each initial state. An alignment contributes the product of its random-phase emission probabilities, or 0 if a checksum position disagrees with the running sum there.

test_vectors.description: P(10101) under the process n=3, m=2 -- a three-bit block plus its parity.
test_vectors.notes: Summed over the 4 phase alignments, weighted by the stationary probability of each initial state. An alignment contributes the product of its random-phase emission probabilities, or 0 if a checksum position disagrees with the running sum there.

test_vectors.description: P(011) from an explicit initial state pinned to the start of a block.
test_vectors.notes: With initial_state pinned to the seed state the phase is known, so only one alignment contributes: probs[0][0] * probs[1][1] = 0.3 * 0.4, with the checksum 0 XOR 1 = 1 matching the third symbol. Exercises the optional initial_state field of SPEC 7.1.1.

test_vectors.description: Stationary distribution of RRXOR leaked toward uniform with epsilon = 0.1.
test_vectors.notes: leak_toward mixes in (epsilon / V) * outer(w, eta) with eta uniform, adding epsilon / (V * S) = 0.1 / (2 * 5) to every entry, so the chain stays row-stochastic and becomes irreducible and aperiodic. No closed form: this is the fixed point of pi = (1 - epsilon) pi T_block + epsilon / S, and it sits closer to uniform than the unleaked [2, 1, 1, 1, 1] / 6.

test_vectors.description: Observation distribution of leaked RRXOR from its stationary state.
test_vectors.notes: Symmetry in both RRXOR and the uniform leak keeps the two symbols equiprobable.

test_vectors.description: State update of leaked RRXOR from its stationary state after observing 0.
test_vectors.notes: Under a leak no state is ruled out, so the posterior has full support -- unlike the unleaked process, where a pure state stays pure and the posterior is a unit vector.

test_vectors.description: P(00100) under leaked RRXOR: positive, where the unleaked process forbids it.
test_vectors.notes: The companion vector checksum_seq_prob_rrxor_forbidden gives exactly 0 for this word. A leak of 0.1 makes it possible, which is the point of the augmentation.
